prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 2 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 12 of 26 earlier cases, t = 0 in 14; when indemnified t per unit about 81 (80% range 73 to 88); revealed per unit: >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34)
- line 6 "Installer hours": no earlier line of this grade; level of the other hourly grades; when indemnified t per hr about 63 (80% range 23 to 176)
- line 8 "Service technician hours": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per hr about 47 (80% range 36 to 69); revealed per hr: 44-49 (case 21), so this line (9 hr) about 425 (327 to 621)
- line 9 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 12 of 26 earlier cases, t = 0 in 14; when indemnified t per pc about 81 (80% range 73 to 88); revealed per pc: >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34)

items.description: Close wall opening and repaint affected area
items.rationale: The indoor supply-line escape is covered under §2.4. Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(a) allow local patching and repainting of the disturbed area, estimated at €320 gross, not repainting of unaffected walls.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge on the contractor’s invoice; one flat-rate charge is estimated at €81 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers sealing consumables used in the pipe repair; €12 gross is reasonable for one small allowance.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow like-for-like material for the failed section; the first metre is estimated at €29 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers reinstatement of pre-existing insulation on the repaired section; one metre is estimated at €13 gross.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers reasonably necessary trade labour; the separate installer hour is estimated at €63 gross.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers necessary investigation, but §7.1.8(b) excludes a separate charge for the contractor’s own measuring device. If documented as qualifying hired drying equipment instead, a small charge of €18 gross is plausible.
Sections 7.1.7(e) and (g) allow necessary investigation and repair labour; the first nine-hour entry is estimated at €425 gross.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows only the first travel charge on this contractor’s invoice, even for multiple visits. A qualifying single vehicle charge would be €81 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(b) and (e) cover one flat-rate deployment for necessary drying; brief drying of the local wall area is estimated at €75 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes the contractor’s blades as business equipment. The conditional gross value of one blade is €9.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers fittings used to reconnect the repaired section; two standard gunmetal fittings at about €19 each total €38 gross.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and (d) exclude repeat or unsupported material charges; no distinct second metre is documented. If verified as separately installed and necessary, it would be €29 gross.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and (d) exclude duplicate or unsupported material; the shell appears to repeat the first metre of insulation. If it served a distinct repaired section, one metre would be €14 gross.

Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(c) bar duplicate labour and limit payment to necessary time; multiple visits do not establish a distinct second nine-hour block. If verified as separate and necessary, nine hours would be €425 gross.
